landmarks.name: Acacia
landmarks.subtitle: Acacia · 2340 Piedmont Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house of the Acacia fraternity on Piedmont Avenue, a white mid-century modern house with a deep framed street front and a roof deck.

landmarks.name: Clark Kerr Administration & Academic Center
landmarks.subtitle: Clark Kerr Campus · Spanish Colonial Revival
landmarks.blurb: Built for the California School for the Deaf and Blind, these stucco and red-tile buildings now hold the Clark Kerr Campus offices and an academic center with study space for residents.

landmarks.name: African American Theme House
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative · 2347 Prospect St
landmarks.blurb: Known as Afro House, this Berkeley Student Cooperative house is a theme house centred on African American culture and community.

landmarks.name: Alpha Chi Omega
landmarks.subtitle: ΑΧΩ · 2313 Warring Street
landmarks.blurb: Alpha Chi Omega chapter house on Warring Street, a flat-roofed cedar-shingled building stepping up the hillside with big wood-framed windows.

landmarks.name: Alpha Chi Sigma
landmarks.subtitle: ΑΧΣ · 2627 Virginia Street
landmarks.blurb: House of the Sigma chapter of Alpha Chi Sigma, the professional chemistry fraternity, a white stucco Spanish Revival house with red tile roofs on the hillside north of campus.

landmarks.name: Alpha Delta Chi
landmarks.subtitle: ΑΔΧ · 2730 Dwight Way
landmarks.blurb: Alpha chapter house of Alpha Delta Chi, the Christian sorority founded at Berkeley in 1925: a lavender Victorian with a flat-roofed front addition carrying the letters.

landmarks.name: Alpha Delta Phi
landmarks.subtitle: ΑΔΦ · 2422 Prospect Street
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house of the California chapter of Alpha Delta Phi, founded at Berkeley in 1908: an asymmetric stucco house on Prospect Street with a steep dormered roof and a front-gabled wing carrying the letters.

landmarks.name: Alpha Delta Pi
landmarks.subtitle: ΑΔΠ · 2400 Piedmont Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house of Alpha Delta Pi at Piedmont Avenue and Channing Way, a half-timbered Tudor Revival house with a steep street gable behind a brick garden wall.

landmarks.name: Alpha Phi
landmarks.subtitle: ΑΦ · 2830 Bancroft Steps
landmarks.blurb: Alpha Phi (Nu chapter) house on the Bancroft Steps, a big brown-shingle house that climbs the hillside toward the stadium.

landmarks.name: Anderson Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Pacific School of Religion · 1811 Arch St
landmarks.blurb: Student residence of the Pacific School of Religion on Holy Hill, north of the UC Berkeley campus.

landmarks.name: Andres Castro Arms
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: Andres Castro Arms, on the hillside at Prospect and Warring streets, is the Berkeley Student Cooperative's Person of Color Theme House.

landmarks.name: Anna Head School
landmarks.subtitle: Soule Edgar Fisher · 1892
landmarks.blurb: The brown-shingle main building of the Anna Head School for Girls, a landmark of the First Bay Tradition; UC Berkeley acquired the campus after the school moved to Oakland in 1964.

landmarks.name: Anthony Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Joseph Esherick · 1957
landmarks.blurb: Built as the offices of the California Pelican, the student humor magazine founded in 1903 by Earle C. Anthony, this small Bay Region building by Strawberry Creek still wears a carved pelican over its door.

landmarks.name: Building 21 (Wilkinson Lodge)
landmarks.subtitle: Alfred Eichler · 1928
landmarks.blurb: Built in 1928 as the boys’ dormitory and dining hall of the California School for the Blind and later named Wilkinson Lodge, this Spanish Colonial Revival building steps up the hillside. It has stood largely vacant since 1979 and is used for storage.

landmarks.name: Aumann Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Lighthaven · 2740 Telegraph
landmarks.blurb: The largest building of Lighthaven, the campus at 2740 Telegraph Avenue (formerly the Rose Garden Inn); named after the game theorist Robert Aumann, it holds common space downstairs and seven bedrooms upstairs.

landmarks.name: Bakar BioEnginuity Hub
landmarks.subtitle: Mario Ciampi · 1970 · renovated 2023
landmarks.blurb: Built as the University Art Museum, Mario Ciampi's brutalist fan of cantilevered concrete galleries reopened in 2023 as the Bakar BioEnginuity Hub, a lab and incubator space for life-science startups.

landmarks.name: Bancroft Parking Structure
landmarks.subtitle: WRNS Studio · 2026
landmarks.blurb: A roughly 660-space UC Berkeley parking structure on Bancroft Way, opened in September 2026 on the site of the former Hearst tennis courts and garage.

landmarks.name: Barker Hall
landmarks.subtitle: 1964 · Life sciences labs
landmarks.blurb: A 1960s concrete laboratory tower named for UC regent Warren Barker, now home to molecular and cell biology research and the Helen Wills Neuroscience Institute.

landmarks.name: Bauer Wurster Hall
landmarks.subtitle: DeMars, Esherick & Olsen · 1964
landmarks.blurb: Home of the College of Environmental Design, Wurster Hall is Berkeley's best-known brutalist building: board-formed concrete left raw, with a ten-storey tower over studio wings wrapped around a courtyard.

landmarks.name: Benton Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Pacific School of Religion
landmarks.blurb: Student residence of the Pacific School of Religion on Holy Hill, north of the UC Berkeley campus.

landmarks.name: Berkeley Art Museum & Pacific Film Archive
landmarks.subtitle: Diller Scofidio + Renfro · 2016
landmarks.blurb: BAMPFA moved downtown in 2016 into the 1939 UC Printing Plant, wrapped by a new stainless-steel volume designed by Diller Scofidio + Renfro, with a large outdoor LED screen for films and video art.

landmarks.name: Berkeley City College
landmarks.subtitle: 2050 Center Street · 2006
landmarks.blurb: One of the four Peralta Community Colleges, Berkeley City College (formerly Vista College) moved into this seven-storey building on Center Street in 2006, a block from Downtown Berkeley BART.

landmarks.name: Berkeley Way West
landmarks.subtitle: KieranTimberlake · 2018
landmarks.blurb: Home to the School of Public Health, the Department of Psychology and the Graduate School of Education, Berkeley Way West opened in 2018.

landmarks.name: Beverly Cleary Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence hall
landmarks.blurb: A residence hall on the Southside named for the children’s author Beverly Cleary, a Berkeley alumna (1938) who wrote the Ramona books.

landmarks.name: The Big C
landmarks.subtitle: Charter Hill · 1905
landmarks.blurb: Built on March 23, 1905 by the classes of 1907 and 1908 to replace the dangerous freshman-sophomore "rush"; a plaque in the letter reads "In memory of the Rush, buried Charter Day 1905 by the classes of 1907 and 1908. Requiescat in pace." The freshmen then painted the concrete gold.

landmarks.name: Birge Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Physics · 1964
landmarks.blurb: Named for Raymond T. Birge, who led Berkeley's physics department for over two decades, this laboratory block joined LeConte Hall to form the physics complex.

landmarks.name: Bowles Hall
landmarks.subtitle: George W. Kelham · 1929
landmarks.blurb: Dedicated in 1929 with a gift from Mary McNear Bowles in memory of her husband, Regent Phillip E. Bowles, this castle-like Collegiate Gothic hall on the hill above Memorial Stadium was the first residence hall on campus.

landmarks.name: Redwood Gardens
landmarks.subtitle: Senior apartments · 1986
landmarks.blurb: A 169-unit senior housing complex in Spanish-style stucco and red tile at 2951 Derby Street, built in the 1980s on the grounds of the former California School for the Blind and surrounded by the Clark Kerr Campus.

landmarks.name: Old Gymnasium (Building 22)
landmarks.subtitle: California School for the Blind · 1914
landmarks.blurb: Built in 1914 as the gymnasium of the California School for the Blind, this cream-painted brick hall is a contributor to the Clark Kerr Campus historic district and now serves as archive storage.

landmarks.name: Pi Kappa Alpha
landmarks.subtitle: ΠΚΑ · 2324 Piedmont Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house of Pi Kappa Alpha on Piedmont Avenue, a grey stucco Craftsman house with deep eaves and a columned entry porch under the letters.

landmarks.name: Delta Delta Delta
landmarks.subtitle: ΔΔΔ · 2300 Warring Street
landmarks.blurb: Tri Delta chapter house at Warring Street and Bancroft Way, a large L-shaped house in pale blue-grey with white trim.

landmarks.name: Alpha Epsilon Pi
landmarks.subtitle: ΑΕΠ · 2430 Piedmont Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house of Alpha Epsilon Pi on Piedmont Avenue, a three-storey stucco block with big blue letters facing the street.

landmarks.name: Delta Sigma
landmarks.subtitle: ΔΣ · 2311 Prospect Street
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house on Prospect Street, a tall cream stucco Spanish Colonial building on the hillside with tile roofs and a rooftop terrace.

landmarks.name: Delta Kappa Epsilon
landmarks.subtitle: ΔΚΕ · 2302 Piedmont Avenue
landmarks.blurb: The DKE house at Piedmont Avenue and Bancroft Way, an Arts-and-Crafts house with a big central gable over Piedmont carrying the letters.

landmarks.name: Sigma Nu
landmarks.subtitle: ΣΝ · 2710 Bancroft Way
landmarks.blurb: Sigma Nu chapter house on Bancroft Way, a two-storey house with a hipped roof and a columned porch facing the street.

landmarks.name: Theta Delta Chi
landmarks.subtitle: ΘΔΧ · 2647 Durant Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house of Theta Delta Chi on Durant Avenue, an ivy-covered Tudor Revival house with a half-timbered front gable.

landmarks.name: Sigma Alpha Epsilon
landmarks.subtitle: ΣΑΕ · 2722 Bancroft Way
landmarks.blurb: Sigma Alpha Epsilon chapter house on Bancroft Way, a Spanish Colonial courtyard house with red tile roofs and a pier arcade.

landmarks.name: Alpha Sigma Phi
landmarks.subtitle: ΑΣΦ · 2498 Piedmont Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Alpha Sigma Phi chapter house at Piedmont Avenue and Dwight Way, a three-storey stucco house with a low tile roof.

landmarks.name: Sigma Chi
landmarks.subtitle: ΣΧ · 2345 College Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Sigma Chi chapter house on College Avenue, a two-storey flat-roofed modern building with long bands of windows.

landmarks.name: Delta Gamma
landmarks.subtitle: ΔΓ · 2710 Channing Way
landmarks.blurb: Delta Gamma chapter house on Channing Way, a large three-storey stucco house with low tile roofs.

landmarks.name: Alpha Tau Omega
landmarks.subtitle: ΑΤΩ · 2327 Warring Street
landmarks.blurb: Alpha Tau Omega chapter house on Warring Street, a three-storey red-brick Georgian Revival house with a white columned portico.

landmarks.name: Zeta Beta Tau
landmarks.subtitle: ΖΒΤ · 2721 Channing Way
landmarks.blurb: Zeta Beta Tau chapter house on Channing Way, a three-storey brick Colonial Revival house with a columned portico.

landmarks.name: Phi Delta Theta
landmarks.subtitle: ΦΔΘ · 2726 Channing Way
landmarks.blurb: Phi Delta Theta house on Channing Way, a cream stucco Mediterranean villa with a red tile roof and a columned loggia.

landmarks.name: Kappa Alpha Theta
landmarks.subtitle: ΚΑΘ · 2723 Durant Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Kappa Alpha Theta (Omega chapter) house on Durant Avenue, a 1920s Mediterranean house whose U-shaped front frames an arched loggia.

landmarks.name: Pi Lambda Phi
landmarks.subtitle: ΠΛΦ · 2727 Channing Way
landmarks.blurb: Pi Lambda Phi chapter house on Channing Way, a three-storey brown-shingle house with a hipped roof and a front porch.

landmarks.name: Chi Phi
landmarks.subtitle: ΧΦ · 2722 Durant Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Chi Phi chapter house on Durant Avenue, a front-gabled brown-shingle house with a full-width porch.

landmarks.name: Sigma Alpha Mu
landmarks.subtitle: ΣΑΜ · 2714 Durant Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house of Sigma Alpha Mu on Durant Avenue, a lap-sided Colonial Revival house with black shutters and a small columned portico.

landmarks.name: Tau Kappa Epsilon
landmarks.subtitle: ΤΚΕ · 2725 Channing Way
landmarks.blurb: Tau Kappa Epsilon chapter house on Channing Way, a three-storey stucco house with a side-gabled roof.

landmarks.name: Phi Kappa Sigma
landmarks.subtitle: ΦΚΣ · 2320 Warring Street
landmarks.blurb: Phi Kappa Sigma chapter house on Warring Street, a long stucco house stepping down the hillside under low roofs.

landmarks.name: Alpha Gamma Omega
landmarks.subtitle: ΑΓΩ · 2713 Haste Street
landmarks.blurb: Alpha Gamma Omega chapter house on Haste Street, a small front-gabled stucco house.

landmarks.name: Vista del Mar
landmarks.subtitle: California School for the Blind · 1924
landmarks.blurb: Completed in 1924 as the Vista del Mar girls’ residence, the first new building of the California School for the Blind after it separated from the School for the Deaf. It faces Derby Street and is now part of the Redwood Gardens senior housing complex.

landmarks.name: C. V. Starr East Asian Library
landmarks.subtitle: Tod Williams Billie Tsien · 2008
landmarks.blurb: The first free-standing East Asian library building in the United States, holding Berkeley's Chinese, Japanese and Korean collections behind a screen of bronze.

landmarks.name: California Hall
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1905
landmarks.blurb: The first building completed under the Phoebe Hearst campus plan, California Hall was built of Raymond granite with a red tile roof as a fireproof home for the university administration. Today it houses the Chancellor's office.

landmarks.name: Calvin Laboratory
landmarks.subtitle: The Roundhouse · 1964
landmarks.blurb: Built for Melvin Calvin's chemical biodynamics group after his 1961 Nobel Prize for mapping the path of carbon in photosynthesis. The round plan was meant to keep researchers in constant contact; today it houses the Simons Institute for the Theory of Computing.

landmarks.name: Campbell Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Astronomy & physics · 2015
landmarks.blurb: Rebuilt in 2015 to replace the seismically unsafe 1959 building of the same name, Campbell Hall houses astronomy and physics research, with a rooftop deck for observing.

landmarks.name: Casa Zimbabwe
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: Known to residents as CZ, this stepped stucco-and-concrete complex on Ridge Road is one of the largest houses of the Berkeley Student Cooperative.

landmarks.name: Channing-Bowditch Apartments
landmarks.subtitle: Student apartments
landmarks.blurb: University student apartments at Channing Way and Bowditch Street, built around the historic Anna Head School buildings.

landmarks.name: Cheney Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 1
landmarks.blurb: One of the four original high-rise towers of Residence Halls Unit 1, the 1960s dormitory complex on the block between Durant Avenue and Channing Way, grouped around a courtyard with a central dining commons.

landmarks.name: Kappa Alpha Order
landmarks.subtitle: ΚΑ · 2425 Piedmont Avenue
landmarks.blurb: The Kappa Alpha Order house on Piedmont Avenue (OpenStreetMap still labels it Chi Omega), a red-brick Georgian Revival house built around a court.

landmarks.name: Chi Omega
landmarks.subtitle: ΧΩ · 2421 Piedmont Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Chi Omega (Mu chapter) house on Piedmont Avenue, a large red-brick Georgian Revival house with a columned entrance under a swan-neck pediment.

landmarks.name: Chou Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Haas School of Business · 2017
landmarks.blurb: Connie & Kevin Chou Hall, the Haas School of Business's North Academic Building, opened in 2017 with classrooms, study space and a rooftop terrace; it was designed as a zero-waste, LEED Platinum building.

landmarks.name: Christian Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 1
landmarks.blurb: A newer residence hall added to Unit 1 in the 2000s, filling the block edge between the 1960s towers with lower, colour-blocked wings, glazed stair and lounge stacks and a ground-floor common area.

landmarks.name: Cloyne Court
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1904
landmarks.blurb: Built in 1904 as the Cloyne Court Hotel, a brown-shingle apartment hotel designed by John Galen Howard, it is now the largest house of the Berkeley Student Cooperative.

landmarks.name: Conference Center
landmarks.subtitle: UC Botanical Garden
landmarks.blurb: A garden meeting hall in the UC Botanical Garden in Strawberry Canyon, next to Julia Morgan Hall.

landmarks.name: Cory Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Electrical Engineering · 1950
landmarks.blurb: Named for Clarence L. Cory, an early dean of engineering at Berkeley, Cory Hall opened around 1950 for electrical engineering and is still a home of Berkeley EECS labs and classrooms.

landmarks.name: Cunningham Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 2
landmarks.blurb: One of the four original high-rise towers of Residence Halls Unit 2, the 1960s dormitory complex between Channing Way and Haste Street; like Unit 1 it groups its towers around a courtyard, and the towers later received exterior seismic bracing.

landmarks.name: d’Autremont Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Pacific School of Religion
landmarks.blurb: A building of the Pacific School of Religion, the Protestant seminary on Holy Hill north of campus.

landmarks.name: David Blackwell Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence hall · 2018
landmarks.blurb: Named for statistician David Blackwell, the first Black tenured professor at UC Berkeley, this eight-storey residence hall opened in 2018.

landmarks.name: Davidson Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 2
landmarks.blurb: One of the four original high-rise towers of Residence Halls Unit 2, the 1960s dormitory complex between Channing Way and Haste Street; like Unit 1 it groups its towers around a courtyard, and the towers later received exterior seismic bracing.

landmarks.name: Davis Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Civil & Environmental Engineering
landmarks.blurb: Home of civil and environmental engineering, with large structural testing laboratories where full-scale beams, columns and walls are loaded to failure. Named for Raymond E. Davis, a pioneer of concrete research.

landmarks.name: Davis House
landmarks.subtitle: Julia Morgan
landmarks.blurb: Designed by Julia Morgan and set on the hillside Bancroft Steps, Davis House is now one of the Berkeley Student Cooperative's houses.

landmarks.name: Delta Sigma Phi
landmarks.subtitle: ΔΣΦ · 2311 Piedmont Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house of the Hilgard chapter of Delta Sigma Phi on Piedmont Avenue: a mid-century wood-clad block set back on a red-brick podium facing the street.

landmarks.name: Delta Upsilon
landmarks.subtitle: ΔΥ · 2425 Warring Street
landmarks.blurb: Delta Upsilon chapter house on Warring Street, a cream stucco Italian Renaissance villa with a red tile roof and an arcaded top-floor loggia.

landmarks.name: Deutsch Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 1
landmarks.blurb: One of the four original high-rise towers of Residence Halls Unit 1, the 1960s dormitory complex on the block between Durant Avenue and Channing Way, grouped around a courtyard with a central dining commons.

landmarks.name: Clark Kerr Dining Center & Suites
landmarks.subtitle: Clark Kerr Campus · Spanish Colonial Revival
landmarks.blurb: The Clark Kerr Campus was built for the California School for the Deaf and Blind and became part of UC Berkeley in 1982; its dining commons occupies a historic 1930s room with outdoor patios.

landmarks.name: Doe Memorial Library
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1911 · with The Bancroft Library
landmarks.blurb: Named for benefactor Charles Franklin Doe, whose 1904 bequest funded it, Howard's granite Beaux-Arts library faces Memorial Glade with sixteen engaged columns framing the arched windows of the North Reading Room. The Bancroft Library, the largest collection on the history of California and western North America, adjoins it on the east.

landmarks.name: Donner Laboratory
landmarks.subtitle: Nuclear medicine · 1941
landmarks.blurb: Funded by William H. Donner for John H. Lawrence's research using radioactive isotopes to diagnose and treat disease, Donner Lab is considered a birthplace of nuclear medicine.

landmarks.name: Downtown Berkeley BART
landmarks.subtitle: Shattuck Ave & Center St · 1973
landmarks.blurb: The subway station under Shattuck Avenue opened in 1973 as Berkeley station and was later renamed Downtown Berkeley. The plaza was rebuilt in 2016-18, replacing the old rotunda with the glass entrance canopy. Walk down any entrance to the concourse and the platform.

landmarks.name: Durant Hall
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1911
landmarks.blurb: Built in 1911 as Boalt Hall of Law, this granite Beaux-Arts hall was renamed for Henry Durant, the University's first president, after the law school moved out in 1951. A pair of Chinese guardian lions flanks its door.

landmarks.name: Durant Residence Hall
landmarks.subtitle: 2731 Durant Avenue
landmarks.blurb: A Berkeley brown-shingle house on Durant Avenue, now used as student housing.

landmarks.name: Dwinelle Hall
landmarks.subtitle: 1952 · Humanities
landmarks.blurb: Named for John W. Dwinelle, author of the 1868 act that created the University of California, this sprawling building of split levels and odd corridors is legendary for getting students lost.

landmarks.name: Cheit Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Haas School of Business · Moore Ruble Yudell, 1995
landmarks.blurb: Named for former Haas dean Earl F. Cheit, the hall is one of the hipped-roof buildings of the Haas School of Business complex, grouped around O'Donnell Courtyard on the hillside at Piedmont Avenue.

landmarks.name: Earl Warren Hall
landmarks.subtitle: 2195 Hearst Avenue · 1955
landmarks.blurb: Named for Earl Warren, Berkeley alumnus, California governor and Chief Justice of the United States. Completed in 1955 and later renovated, it houses campus research computing and the university data center.

landmarks.name: Edwards Stadium
landmarks.subtitle: Track & field and soccer · 1932
landmarks.blurb: Opened in 1932 and named for mathematics professor George C. Edwards, the concrete stadium has hosted NCAA championships and a string of track world records; Cal soccer plays on Goldman Field inside the oval.

landmarks.name: Ehrman Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 2
landmarks.blurb: One of the four original high-rise towers of Residence Halls Unit 2, the 1960s dormitory complex between Channing Way and Haste Street; like Unit 1 it groups its towers around a courtyard, and the towers later received exterior seismic bracing.

landmarks.name: Ellsworth Parking Structure
landmarks.subtitle: Parking structure · rooftop tennis courts
landmarks.blurb: A UC Berkeley parking structure south of campus between Haste and Channing, with nine tennis courts on its roof.

landmarks.name: Eshleman Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Moore Ruble Yudell · 2015
landmarks.blurb: Rebuilt in 2015 as part of the Lower Sproul redevelopment, Eshleman Hall houses the ASUC student government and hundreds of student organizations on the south side of Lower Sproul Plaza.

landmarks.name: Etcheverry Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill · 1964
landmarks.blurb: Named for Bernard Etcheverry, a pioneer of irrigation engineering, this long concrete-and-brick slab on Hearst Avenue houses mechanical and nuclear engineering and, for decades, the campus research reactor.

landmarks.name: Euclid Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: A Berkeley Student Cooperative house on Euclid Avenue, a short walk from North Gate.

landmarks.name: Evans Diamond
landmarks.subtitle: Cal baseball · since 1933
landmarks.blurb: Cal baseball has played at Evans Diamond since 1933; the field is named for Edwin Evans and the ballpark for longtime supporter Stu Gordon. Right field backs onto Edwards Stadium and left field onto Haas Pavilion.

landmarks.name: Evans Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Gardner Dailey · 1971
landmarks.blurb: Home to mathematics, statistics and economics. Before Soda Hall opened, computer science was housed here too, and Berkeley Unix (BSD) was developed in its machine rooms. Its grey-green brutalist concrete has been loved and loathed for half a century.

landmarks.name: Evans Manor (Barrington Hall)
landmarks.subtitle: 2315 Dwight Way
landmarks.blurb: Barrington Hall was one of the largest and most famous houses of the Berkeley Student Cooperative from 1935 until 1990; the building is now private apartments known as Evans Manor.

landmarks.name: Faculty Apartments
landmarks.subtitle: Clark Kerr Campus
landmarks.blurb: White-stucco, red-tile apartments on the Clark Kerr Campus, the former California School for the Deaf and Blind, now part of UC Berkeley.

landmarks.name: Faculty Apartments
landmarks.subtitle: Clark Kerr Campus
landmarks.blurb: White-stucco, red-tile apartments on the Clark Kerr Campus, the former California School for the Deaf and Blind, now part of UC Berkeley.

landmarks.name: The Faculty Club
landmarks.subtitle: Bernard Maybeck · 1902
landmarks.blurb: Bernard Maybeck designed the original clubhouse, with its timber-trussed Great Hall, in 1902; the club has grown in stages since, a cream stucco and red-tile cluster tucked among the trees of Faculty Glade by Strawberry Creek.

landmarks.name: Faculty House
landmarks.subtitle: Clark Kerr Campus
landmarks.blurb: A small white-stucco, red-tile house on the edge of the Clark Kerr Campus, the former California School for the Deaf and Blind.

landmarks.name: Fenwick Weavers' Village
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: Fenwick Weavers’ Village is a Berkeley Student Cooperative apartment complex on Dwight Way, three-storey wings of apartments wrapped around landscaped courtyards next to Rochdale Village.

landmarks.name: Foothill · Hillside 4
landmarks.subtitle: William Turnbull Jr. · 1991
landmarks.blurb: Foothill’s shingled residence halls step up the hillside along Hearst Avenue and La Loma like a small village of linked houses, joined by bridges, stairs and courts; a Bay Region style design by William Turnbull Jr.

landmarks.name: Foothill · Hillside 5
landmarks.subtitle: William Turnbull Jr. · 1991
landmarks.blurb: Foothill’s shingled residence halls step up the hillside along Hearst Avenue and La Loma like a small village of linked houses, joined by bridges, stairs and courts; a Bay Region style design by William Turnbull Jr.

landmarks.name: Foothill · Hillside 6–8
landmarks.subtitle: William Turnbull Jr. · 1991
landmarks.blurb: Foothill’s shingled residence halls step up the hillside along Hearst Avenue and La Loma like a small village of linked houses, joined by bridges, stairs and courts; a Bay Region style design by William Turnbull Jr.

landmarks.name: Foothill · Hillside 9
landmarks.subtitle: William Turnbull Jr. · 1991
landmarks.blurb: Foothill’s shingled residence halls step up the hillside along Hearst Avenue and La Loma like a small village of linked houses, joined by bridges, stairs and courts; a Bay Region style design by William Turnbull Jr.

landmarks.name: Foothill · La Loma 1
landmarks.subtitle: William Turnbull Jr. · 1991
landmarks.blurb: Foothill’s shingled residence halls step up the hillside at Hearst and La Loma like a small village of linked houses, a Bay Region style design by William Turnbull Jr.

landmarks.name: Foothill · La Loma 2
landmarks.subtitle: William Turnbull Jr. · 1991
landmarks.blurb: Foothill’s shingled residence halls step up the hillside along Hearst Avenue and La Loma like a small village of linked houses, joined by bridges, stairs and courts; a Bay Region style design by William Turnbull Jr.

landmarks.name: Foothill · La Loma 3
landmarks.subtitle: William Turnbull Jr. · 1991
landmarks.blurb: Foothill’s shingled residence halls step up the hillside along Hearst Avenue and La Loma like a small village of linked houses, joined by bridges, stairs and courts; a Bay Region style design by William Turnbull Jr.

landmarks.name: Founders Building
landmarks.subtitle: Tang Center · 1993
landmarks.blurb: A small single-storey building completed in 1993 beside the Tang Center, home of University Health Services.

landmarks.name: Freeborn Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 1
landmarks.blurb: One of the four original high-rise towers of Residence Halls Unit 1, the 1960s dormitory complex on the block between Durant Avenue and Channing Way, grouped around a courtyard with a central dining commons.

landmarks.name: Gamma Phi Beta
landmarks.subtitle: ΓΦΒ · 2732 Channing Way
landmarks.blurb: Home since 1937 of the Eta chapter of Gamma Phi Beta, installed at Berkeley in 1894: a pale stucco house whose two wings frame a small entrance court on Channing Way.

landmarks.name: Garden Village
landmarks.subtitle: Stanley Saitowitz · 2016
landmarks.blurb: Student housing at 2201 Dwight Way designed by Stanley Saitowitz, built as a cluster of separate boxes linked by bridges, with gardens on the roofs.

landmarks.name: Genetics & Plant Biology Greenhouse
landmarks.subtitle: Research greenhouses
landmarks.blurb: Research greenhouses on Oxford Street serving the plant and microbial biology laboratories.

landmarks.name: Genetics and Plant Biology
landmarks.subtitle: 1990 · Plant & microbial biology
landmarks.blurb: A low stucco and red-tile laboratory building at the north-west corner of campus, used for plant and microbial biology research.

landmarks.name: Gerson Bakar Faculty Building
landmarks.subtitle: Haas School of Business · 1995
landmarks.blurb: The faculty office wing of the Haas School of Business complex, designed by Moore Ruble Yudell with hipped roofs and bracketed eaves that echo Berkeley’s Arts-and-Crafts hillside architecture.

landmarks.name: Giannini Hall
landmarks.subtitle: William C. Hays · 1930
landmarks.blurb: Funded by Bank of Italy founder A. P. Giannini for the Giannini Foundation of Agricultural Economics, the hall closes the west side of the agricultural group.

landmarks.name: Giauque Hall
landmarks.subtitle: College of Chemistry
landmarks.blurb: Named for William F. Giauque, the Berkeley chemist who won the 1949 Nobel Prize for his work on the behaviour of substances at extremely low temperatures.

landmarks.name: Gibbs Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Church Divinity School of the Pacific
landmarks.blurb: Part of the Church Divinity School of the Pacific, the Episcopal seminary on Holy Hill north of campus.

landmarks.name: Gilman Hall
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1917
landmarks.blurb: Glenn Seaborg's team first identified plutonium here in 1941, in Room 307. The chemistry building is a National Historic Landmark.

landmarks.name: Golden Bear Building
landmarks.subtitle: 1995 University Avenue
landmarks.blurb: A downtown office building on University Avenue used by UC Berkeley departments, with shops at street level.

landmarks.name: Golden Bear Café
landmarks.subtitle: César E. Chávez Student Center · DeMars & Hardison · 1960
landmarks.blurb: Built in 1960 as the Golden Bear Restaurant of the new Student Center, this DeMars & Hardison building is roofed by a grid of concrete inverted-pyramid umbrellas. The café faces Upper Sproul Plaza; the César E. Chávez Student Center wing frames the north side of Lower Sproul.

landmarks.name: Golden Bear Recreation Center Gym
landmarks.subtitle: Howson Gymnasium · 1955
landmarks.blurb: Built in 1955 as Howson Gymnasium for the California School for the Deaf, this hall is now part of UC Berkeley’s Golden Bear Recreation Center on the Clark Kerr Campus and is home to the Golden Bear Gymnastics program.

landmarks.name: Golden Bear Recreation Center
landmarks.subtitle: Field, track and courts · Clark Kerr Campus
landmarks.blurb: The recreation fields of the Clark Kerr Campus: a running track around a grass field, tennis and sand volleyball courts and an outdoor pool, run by Cal Recreational Sports.

landmarks.name: Goldman Field
landmarks.subtitle: Cal soccer · inside Edwards Stadium
landmarks.blurb: The grass soccer pitch inside the Edwards Stadium track, home of the Cal men's and women's soccer teams.

landmarks.name: Hearst Greek Theatre
landmarks.subtitle: 1903 · John Galen Howard · 8,500 seats
landmarks.blurb: Modeled on the ancient theatre at Epidaurus and paid for by William Randolph Hearst, it was the first of John Galen Howard's campus buildings to be completed. Theodore Roosevelt gave the commencement address here in May 1903, before it was finished.

landmarks.name: Griffiths Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 2
landmarks.blurb: One of the four original high-rise towers of Residence Halls Unit 2, the 1960s dormitory complex between Channing Way and Haste Street; like Unit 1 it groups its towers around a courtyard, and the towers later received exterior seismic bracing.

landmarks.name: Grimes Engineering Center
landmarks.subtitle: SOM · 2025
landmarks.blurb: SOM transformed the 1980 Bechtel Engineering Center into this student hub by setting a glass-and-steel pavilion on the old concrete base. The zig-zag rods around its perimeter carry shape-memory-alloy cables that pull the building back into shape after an earthquake.

landmarks.name: Haas Clubhouse
landmarks.subtitle: Strawberry Canyon Recreational Area
landmarks.blurb: The clubhouse of the Strawberry Canyon Recreational Area, beside the outdoor pool in the wooded canyon above campus, with its sun deck looking over the water.

landmarks.name: Haas Pavilion
landmarks.subtitle: Harmon Gym 1933 · rebuilt 1999
landmarks.blurb: Home of Cal basketball and volleyball, Haas Pavilion was built inside the walls of the 1933 Harmon Gymnasium; the 1999 rebuild added a new upper bowl and roof, roughly doubling its seating to about 11,800.

landmarks.name: Norton House
landmarks.subtitle: Hillegass-Parker House · Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: The Hal and Audrey Norton House on Hillegass Avenue is part of Hillegass-Parker House, a Berkeley Student Cooperative house.

landmarks.name: Hargrove Music Library
landmarks.subtitle: Mack Scogin Merrill Elam · 2004
landmarks.blurb: The Jean Gray Hargrove Music Library holds UC Berkeley's collections of scores, recordings and music manuscripts in a slate- and concrete-clad building beside Morrison Hall.

landmarks.name: Haviland Hall
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1924
landmarks.blurb: Built for the School of Education, this cream Beaux-Arts hall with its small Ionic portico and red tile roofs now houses the School of Social Welfare.

landmarks.name: Hearst Field Annex
landmarks.subtitle: Bancroft Way
landmarks.blurb: A long single-storey wood-frame building next to Hearst Gym, one of the plain "temporary" structures that housed campus programs for decades.

landmarks.name: Hearst Memorial Gymnasium
landmarks.subtitle: Bernard Maybeck & Julia Morgan · 1927
landmarks.blurb: Built as the Hearst Gymnasium for Women in memory of Phoebe Apperson Hearst, Maybeck and Morgan's buff concrete temple of exercise wraps its gyms around raised outdoor terrace pools, ringed with balustrades and urns.

landmarks.name: Hearst Memorial Mining Building
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1907
landmarks.blurb: Phoebe Apperson Hearst paid for this Beaux-Arts building in memory of her husband, Senator George Hearst, who made his fortune in mining; it was dedicated on August 23, 1907. Behind the three great arches of its south front, Guastavino-tiled domes 50 feet up light the memorial vestibule, and a 1998–2003 seismic retrofit set the whole building on an isolation platform that allows up to a metre of sideways travel.

landmarks.name: Hellman Tennis Complex
landmarks.subtitle: Cal Tennis · six courts beside Edwards Stadium
landmarks.blurb: Home courts of the Cal men's and women's tennis teams: a row of six hard courts at the corner of Oxford Street and Bancroft Way, next to Edwards Stadium.

landmarks.name: Hertz Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Gardner Dailey · 1958
landmarks.blurb: The Department of Music's concert hall, named for benefactor Alfred Hertz, seats about 680 and hosts the University Symphony, chamber concerts and Cal Performances events.

landmarks.name: Hesse Hall
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1924
landmarks.blurb: Built in 1924 for mechanical engineering and named for Frederick Godfrey Hesse, founder of the College of Mechanics. It housed motor, generator, radio and testing laboratories for the growing college.

landmarks.name: Hildebrand Hall
landmarks.subtitle: College of Chemistry · 1966
landmarks.blurb: Named for chemist Joel H. Hildebrand, who taught at Berkeley for more than seventy years, the building holds chemistry laboratories and the chemistry library.

landmarks.name: Hilgard Hall
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1917
landmarks.blurb: Named for soil scientist Eugene W. Hilgard, it is famous for its colourful sgraffito frieze of agricultural motifs and the inscription "To rescue for human society the native values of rural life."

landmarks.name: Hillegass-Parker House
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: Hillegass-Parker House, at the corner of Hillegass Avenue and Parker Street, is one of the Berkeley Student Cooperative's Southside houses.

landmarks.name: Hillside Club
landmarks.subtitle: John White · 1924
landmarks.blurb: Founded in 1898 to promote building in harmony with the Berkeley hills, the Hillside Club lost its 1906 Maybeck-designed clubhouse in the 1923 fire; the present shingled hall was designed by John White, Maybeck's brother-in-law.

landmarks.name: Howard Hall Apartments
landmarks.subtitle: 2330 Warring Street
landmarks.blurb: A mid-century apartment building of eleven flats on Warring Street, between the south-side fraternity blocks and the Clark Kerr Campus.

landmarks.name: Hoyt Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: A Berkeley Student Cooperative house on Ridge Road, in the cluster of co-ops on Northside just above campus.

landmarks.name: Ida Louise Jackson Graduate House
landmarks.subtitle: Graduate housing · 2002
landmarks.blurb: Renamed in 2004 for educator Ida Louise Jackson, an early African-American graduate of Cal, this graduate residence was the first UC Berkeley building named for an African-American woman.

landmarks.name: Ida Sproul Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 3
landmarks.blurb: One of the four high-rise towers of Residence Halls Unit 3 on Durant Avenue, the last of the Southside 'Units' of the 1960s; its residents eat at Cafe 3.

landmarks.name: Innovative Genomics Institute
landmarks.subtitle: 2151 Berkeley Way · 2012
landmarks.blurb: Opened in 2012 as the Energy Biosciences Building, it is now home to the Innovative Genomics Institute founded by Jennifer Doudna to apply CRISPR genome editing.

landmarks.name: International House
landmarks.subtitle: George W. Kelham · 1930
landmarks.blurb: Built with a gift from John D. Rockefeller Jr., I-House opened in 1930 as a residence where American and international students live together. Its domed tower above Piedmont Avenue is one of the best-known silhouettes on the east side of campus.

landmarks.name: Jacobs Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Jacobs Institute for Design Innovation · 2015
landmarks.blurb: A 24,000-square-foot maker space for design and engineering students, with studios, a fabrication shop, laser cutters and 3D printers. It opened in 2015 on the north side next to Soda Hall.

landmarks.name: Julia Morgan Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Julia Morgan · 1911
landmarks.blurb: Designed by Julia Morgan in 1911 as Girton Hall, a gathering place for Berkeley’s women students, this redwood Arts and Crafts hall was moved from central campus to the UC Botanical Garden, where it is now Julia Morgan Hall.

landmarks.name: Kappa Delta Rho
landmarks.subtitle: ΚΔΡ · 2739 Channing Way
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house of the Lambda chapter of Kappa Delta Rho on Channing Way, a cream stucco Mediterranean house with an arched, columned entry under the fraternity letters.

landmarks.name: Kappa Kappa Gamma
landmarks.subtitle: ΚΚΓ · 2328 Piedmont Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house of the Pi Deuteron chapter of Kappa Kappa Gamma on Piedmont Avenue, a blue-grey Colonial Revival house with a columned portico and dormered hipped roof.

landmarks.name: Kappa Sigma
landmarks.subtitle: ΚΣ · 2400 Warring Street
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house of the Beta Xi chapter of Kappa Sigma at Warring Street and Channing Way, a mid-century modern box raised over an open, pier-supported ground floor.

landmarks.name: Kidd Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: One of the Berkeley Student Cooperative's smaller houses, on Le Conte Avenue on Northside.

landmarks.name: Kingman Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Former Theta Xi house
landmarks.blurb: Built as the Theta Xi fraternity house and now a Berkeley Student Cooperative house, Kingman Hall is known for its terraced hillside garden amphitheatre and the murals inside.

landmarks.name: Koshland Hall
landmarks.subtitle: 1991 · Plant & microbial biology
landmarks.blurb: Named for biochemist Daniel E. Koshland Jr., this laboratory building takes its stucco walls and red tile roofs from the neighbouring agricultural halls.

landmarks.name: Lambda Phi Epsilon
landmarks.subtitle: ΛΦΕ · 2312 Warring Street
landmarks.blurb: Lambda Phi Epsilon is Berkeley's Asian-interest fraternity (Delta chapter, founded 1988); its rush has been held at this 1958 house at 2312 Warring Street.

landmarks.name: Latimer Hall
landmarks.subtitle: College of Chemistry · 1963
landmarks.blurb: The tallest of the chemistry buildings, with teaching and research laboratories stacked eight storeys high beside the round Pimentel lecture hall.

landmarks.name: Lawrence Hall of Science
landmarks.subtitle: Public science center · 1968
landmarks.blurb: Named for Nobel laureate Ernest O. Lawrence, UC Berkeley's public science center opened in 1968 high in the hills above campus. Out on its plaza overlooking the bay, kids climb on Pheena, a life-size fin whale, and a giant DNA double helix.

landmarks.name: Levine-Fricke Field
landmarks.subtitle: Cal Softball · Strawberry Canyon
landmarks.blurb: The home field of Cal Softball, tucked into Strawberry Canyon between Witter Rugby Field and the Strawberry Canyon pool.

landmarks.name: Lewis Hall
landmarks.subtitle: College of Chemistry · 1948
landmarks.blurb: Named for Gilbert N. Lewis, the dean who built Berkeley's College of Chemistry into a powerhouse and devised the electron-pair theory of the chemical bond.

landmarks.name: Li Ka Shing Center
landmarks.subtitle: 2011 · Biomedical & health sciences
landmarks.blurb: Funded in part by Hong Kong businessman Li Ka-shing, this laboratory building houses biomedical and health-sciences research, including stem-cell and neuroscience labs.

landmarks.name: Lothlorien (North House)
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: Lothlorien, named after the elven forest in The Lord of the Rings, is a Berkeley Student Cooperative house made up of two houses sharing a garden on Prospect Street.

landmarks.name: Lothlorien (South House)
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: The south house of Lothlorien, a Berkeley Student Cooperative house on Prospect Street named after the elven forest in The Lord of the Rings.

landmarks.name: Lower Hearst Structure
landmarks.subtitle: Parking structure · 694 spaces
landmarks.blurb: A four-level UC Berkeley parking structure on Hearst Avenue on the north side of campus, with public pay parking on Level 2.

landmarks.name: Ludwig's Fountain
landmarks.subtitle: Sproul Plaza · named 1961
landmarks.blurb: Named by the Regents in 1961 for Ludwig von Schwarenburg, a German short-haired pointer who spent his days wading in this fountain and chasing tennis balls thrown by students. It was the first place on campus named after an animal.

landmarks.name: Main Stacks
landmarks.subtitle: Esherick Homsey Dodge & Davis · 1994
landmarks.blurb: The Gardner (Main) Stacks hold most of the library's collection in four storeys built underground between Doe and Moffitt libraries; the roof is a landscaped terrace.

landmarks.name: Martin Luther King Jr. Student Union
landmarks.subtitle: DeMars & Reay · 1961 · renovated 2015
landmarks.blurb: The ASUC Student Union, renamed for Martin Luther King Jr. in 1985, houses the Cal Student Store and student organizations between Upper and Lower Sproul Plaza. It was renovated and reclad in 2015 as part of the Lower Sproul redevelopment.

landmarks.name: Maximo Martinez Commons
landmarks.subtitle: Haste Street · 2012
landmarks.blurb: A student apartment complex on Haste Street around a landscaped courtyard, with cedar-clad and white-panelled volumes over a glazed ground floor.

landmarks.name: McCone Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Earth & Planetary Science · Geography
landmarks.blurb: Home of the Department of Earth and Planetary Science and the Department of Geography, named for John A. McCone. A long cream concrete slab with a deep floating roof slab.

landmarks.name: McEnerney Hall (CNMAT)
landmarks.subtitle: 1750 Arch Street
landmarks.blurb: Genevieve McEnerney Hall houses UC Berkeley's Center for New Music and Audio Technologies (CNMAT) in a Mediterranean-style villa on Arch Street.

landmarks.name: McLaughlin Hall
landmarks.subtitle: William C. Hays · 1931
landmarks.blurb: A simple classical building of the early 1930s by William C. Hays, part of the College of Engineering complex beside the Hearst Mining Circle, with "ENGINEERING" carved high on its walls.

landmarks.name: California Memorial Stadium
landmarks.subtitle: 1923 · John Galen Howard · on the Hayward Fault
landmarks.blurb: Built in 1923 as a memorial to Californians who died in World War I, with a neoclassical wall modeled on the Roman Colosseum. The Hayward Fault crosses both end zones diagonally, so the 2010-2012 retrofit split the bowl into separate blocks and hung a 375-foot press box over the west stands.

landmarks.name: Minor Hall Addition
landmarks.subtitle: School of Optometry
landmarks.blurb: The School of Optometry's addition beside Minor Hall, holding clinics, teaching labs and research space.

landmarks.name: Minor Hall
landmarks.subtitle: School of Optometry · 1941
landmarks.blurb: Home of Berkeley's Herbert Wertheim School of Optometry and Vision Science. The building is named for Ralph S. Minor, a physicist who helped found optometry instruction at Berkeley.

landmarks.name: Moffitt Undergraduate Library
landmarks.subtitle: John Carl Warnecke · 1970 · renovated 2026
landmarks.blurb: The undergraduate library beside Memorial Glade, linked underground to the Main Stacks. Its top two floors became a 24-hour study space in 2016, and its lower three floors reopened in August 2026 as the Carol T. Christ Center for Connected Learning, with an expanded Free Speech Movement Café at the south entrance.

landmarks.name: Morgan Hall
landmarks.subtitle: 1953 · Nutritional Sciences
landmarks.blurb: Morgan Hall houses the Department of Nutritional Sciences and Toxicology; its stucco walls and red tile roofs echo the older agricultural buildings around it.

landmarks.name: Morrison Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Gardner Dailey · 1958
landmarks.blurb: Home of the Department of Music, Morrison Hall holds classrooms, practice rooms and offices beside Hertz Hall; it is named for May T. Morrison, whose bequest funded the music buildings.

landmarks.name: Mulford Hall
landmarks.subtitle: 1948 · Forestry
landmarks.blurb: Built for the School of Forestry and named for forestry professor Walter Mulford, the hall is known for its interior panelled in many species of wood.

landmarks.name: North Gate Hall
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1906
landmarks.blurb: Built in 1906 as the temporary home of the architecture department, which affectionately called it "the Ark", this brown-shingle Arts & Crafts building now houses the Graduate School of Journalism.

landmarks.name: Norton Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 3
landmarks.blurb: One of the four high-rise towers of Residence Halls Unit 3 on Durant Avenue, the last of the Southside 'Units' of the 1960s; its residents eat at Cafe 3.

landmarks.name: O'Brien Breezeway
landmarks.subtitle: College of Engineering
landmarks.blurb: A glazed two-level walkway over an open ground-floor passage, linking buildings of the College of Engineering complex.

landmarks.name: O'Brien Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Van Bourg & Nakamura · 1959
landmarks.blurb: A modernist three-storey engineering building joined to the east side of Hesse Hall, named in 1968 for Morrough O'Brien, a professor who served as dean of the College of Engineering from 1948 to 1959.

landmarks.name: Old Art Gallery
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1904
landmarks.blurb: Built in 1904 as the campus power house and later the University Art Gallery, this brick hall by John Galen Howard is known for the WPA-era mosaic murals set into its façade.

landmarks.name: Oscar Wilde House
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: Oscar Wilde House on Warring Street is the Berkeley Student Cooperative's LGBTQ+ theme house.

landmarks.name: Oxford Research Unit
landmarks.subtitle: Research greenhouses
landmarks.blurb: The Oxford Tract research greenhouses on the west edge of campus, where plant and microbial biology experiments are grown.

landmarks.name: Panoramic Northside
landmarks.subtitle: 1752 Shattuck Avenue
landmarks.blurb: A new seven-storey apartment building on North Shattuck Avenue at Francisco Street.

landmarks.name: Parsons Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Church Divinity School of the Pacific
landmarks.blurb: A residence hall of the Church Divinity School of the Pacific, the Episcopal seminary on Holy Hill.

landmarks.name: Phi Gamma Delta (Fiji)
landmarks.subtitle: ΦΓΔ · 2395 Piedmont Avenue · Frederick H. Reimers, 1928
landmarks.blurb: Brick Mediterranean-style chapter house at the Piedmont Avenue and Channing Way circle, designed by Frederick H. Reimers in 1928 as the Sigma Pi house and later home of Phi Gamma Delta's Delta Xi chapter.

landmarks.name: Phi Kappa Psi
landmarks.subtitle: ΦΚΨ · 2424 Warring Street
landmarks.blurb: Phi Kappa Psi (California Gamma) chapter house on Warring Street, a flat-roofed mid-century building with brick walls and long bronze-framed window bands.

landmarks.name: Phi Kappa Tau
landmarks.subtitle: ΦΚΤ · 2335 Piedmont Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Home of the Nu chapter of Phi Kappa Tau, at 2335 Piedmont Avenue since 1923.

landmarks.name: Physics North & Physics South
landmarks.subtitle: Former LeConte Hall · John Galen Howard, 1924
landmarks.blurb: Berkeley's physics building, where Ernest Lawrence developed the cyclotron in the early 1930s. Long named LeConte Hall, its two wings were renamed Physics North and Physics South in 2020.

landmarks.name: Pi Beta Phi
landmarks.subtitle: ΠΒΦ · 2325 Piedmont Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house of the California Beta chapter of Pi Beta Phi on Piedmont Avenue, a large half-timbered Tudor Revival house behind a brick garden wall.

landmarks.name: Former Pi Kappa Phi House
landmarks.subtitle: ΠΚΦ · 2908 Channing Way
landmarks.blurb: A three-storey mid-century stucco chapter house at Channing Way and Prospect Street, long home to Pi Kappa Phi, with the letters stacked on its corner wall.

landmarks.name: Pimentel Hall
landmarks.subtitle: College of Chemistry lecture hall · 1964
landmarks.blurb: The round brick lecture hall of the College of Chemistry, named for chemist George C. Pimentel. Its auditorium uses a rotating stage so one demonstration can be set up while another class is under way.

landmarks.name: Priestley Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 3
landmarks.blurb: One of the four high-rise towers of Residence Halls Unit 3 on Durant Avenue, the last of the Southside 'Units' of the 1960s; its residents eat at Cafe 3.

landmarks.name: Putnam Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 1
landmarks.blurb: One of the four original high-rise towers of Residence Halls Unit 1, the 1960s dormitory complex on the block between Durant Avenue and Channing Way, grouped around a courtyard with a central dining commons.

landmarks.name: Tilden Vocational Building
landmarks.subtitle: Langhorst, Kirby & Mulvin · 1952
landmarks.blurb: Built in 1952 as the vocational shops of the California School for the Deaf, this saw-tooth-roofed building was the campus’s first departure from its Spanish Colonial Revival style. It now serves the Clark Kerr Campus as archive and maintenance space.

landmarks.name: Recreational Sports Facility
landmarks.subtitle: 2301 Bancroft Way · 1984
landmarks.blurb: The RSF is the main campus gym, with basketball and volleyball courts, weight rooms and fitness studios, next to the Spieker Aquatics Complex.

landmarks.name: Clark Kerr Campus Residence Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Clark Kerr Campus
landmarks.blurb: One of the Spanish Colonial Revival buildings of the Clark Kerr Campus, the former California Schools for the Deaf and Blind, which UC Berkeley turned into a residential campus at the foot of the hills.

landmarks.name: Clark Kerr Campus Residence Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Clark Kerr Campus
landmarks.blurb: One of the Spanish Colonial Revival buildings of the Clark Kerr Campus, the former California Schools for the Deaf and Blind, which UC Berkeley turned into a residential campus at the foot of the hills.

landmarks.name: Clark Kerr Residence Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Clark Kerr Campus · Spanish Colonial Revival
landmarks.blurb: One of the white-stucco, red-tile residence halls of the Clark Kerr Campus, the former California School for the Deaf and Blind, now UC Berkeley student housing.

landmarks.name: Clark Kerr Residence Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Clark Kerr Campus · Spanish Colonial Revival
landmarks.blurb: One of the white-stucco, red-tile residence halls of the Clark Kerr Campus, the former California School for the Deaf and Blind, now UC Berkeley student housing.

landmarks.name: Clark Kerr Campus Residence Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Clark Kerr Campus
landmarks.blurb: One of the Spanish Colonial Revival buildings of the Clark Kerr Campus, the former California Schools for the Deaf and Blind, which UC Berkeley turned into a residential campus at the foot of the hills.

landmarks.name: Clark Kerr Residence Pavilion
landmarks.subtitle: Clark Kerr Campus · Spanish Colonial Revival
landmarks.blurb: A low white-stucco, red-tile pavilion among the Clark Kerr Campus residence halls, the former California School for the Deaf and Blind.

landmarks.name: Clark Kerr Residence Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Clark Kerr Campus · Spanish Colonial Revival
landmarks.blurb: One of the white-stucco, red-tile residence halls of the Clark Kerr Campus, the former California School for the Deaf and Blind, now UC Berkeley student housing.

landmarks.name: 2455 Prospect Street
landmarks.subtitle: Student housing
landmarks.blurb: A large house on Prospect Street near Dwight Way, now rented as shared student rooms.

landmarks.name: 2399 Prospect Street
landmarks.subtitle: Student housing
landmarks.blurb: A large early-1900s house on Prospect Street, south-east of campus, divided into shared student housing.

landmarks.name: 2425 Prospect Street
landmarks.subtitle: The Prospect · student housing
landmarks.blurb: A large former fraternity-style house on Prospect Street, now a co-living student residence.

landmarks.name: 2479 Le Conte Avenue
landmarks.subtitle: Residence hall
landmarks.blurb: A three-storey residence hall at 2479 Le Conte Avenue on Holy Hill, north of campus.

landmarks.name: 2626 Warring Street
landmarks.subtitle: Julia Morgan house
landmarks.blurb: A large brown-shingle house on Warring Street attributed to Julia Morgan, now used as shared student housing near the Clark Kerr Campus.

landmarks.name: Residential & Student Services Building
landmarks.subtitle: Crossroads dining commons
landmarks.blurb: The Residential and Student Services Building on Channing Way at Bowditch Street houses Crossroads, the largest of the campus dining commons, with housing and student-services offices on the floors above.

landmarks.name: Ridge House
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: A cream stucco co-op house on Ridge Road, neighbour of Casa Zimbabwe, run by the Berkeley Student Cooperative.

landmarks.name: Rochdale Apartments
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: Rochdale Apartments on Haste Street are part of the Berkeley Student Cooperative’s Rochdale Village, named after the Rochdale Pioneers who founded the modern co-operative movement in 1844.

landmarks.name: Rochdale Village Building B
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: One of the wood-sided garden-apartment buildings of the Berkeley Student Cooperative’s Rochdale Village, set around a landscaped courtyard south of Haste Street.

landmarks.name: Rochdale Village Building C
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: One of the wood-sided garden-apartment buildings of the Berkeley Student Cooperative’s Rochdale Village, set around a landscaped courtyard south of Haste Street.

landmarks.name: Rochdale Village Building D
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: One of the wood-sided garden-apartment buildings of the Berkeley Student Cooperative’s Rochdale Village, set around a landscaped courtyard south of Haste Street.

landmarks.name: Rochdale Village Building E
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: One of the wood-sided garden-apartment buildings of the Berkeley Student Cooperative’s Rochdale Village, set around a landscaped courtyard south of Haste Street.

landmarks.name: Sather Gate
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1910
landmarks.blurb: Given by Jane K. Sather in memory of her husband Peder, this granite and bronze gate was once the formal southern entrance to campus. Its eight marble reliefs by Earl Cummings were taken down over objections to their nudity and reinstalled in the 1970s; the gate framed the Free Speech Movement's 1964 protests.

landmarks.name: Sather Tower
landmarks.subtitle: The Campanile · 307 feet · 1914
landmarks.blurb: John Galen Howard's granite clock and bell tower, a gift of Jane K. Sather modelled on St. Mark's Campanile in Venice. An elevator rises to the open observation deck 200 feet up, which shares the belfry with a 61-bell carillon; the four clock dials are 17 feet across.

landmarks.name: Senior Hall
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1906
landmarks.blurb: Built of redwood logs for the senior men of the class of 1906, the cabin is the meeting place of the Order of the Golden Bear and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

landmarks.name: Sherman Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: A Berkeley Student Cooperative house on Prospect Street beside the Bancroft Steps, a few minutes' walk from Memorial Stadium.

landmarks.name: Sigma Kappa
landmarks.subtitle: ΣΚ · 2409 Warring Street
landmarks.blurb: Sigma Kappa chapter house on Warring Street, a pale pink stucco house with steep gables, arched openings and a terrace.

landmarks.name: Thorsen House (Sigma Phi)
landmarks.subtitle: ΣΦ · 2307 Piedmont Avenue · Greene & Greene, 1909
landmarks.blurb: The William R. Thorsen House, designed by Charles and Henry Greene in 1909 and home of the Sigma Phi Society since 1942; a National Historic Landmark-quality Arts & Crafts house of shingle, redwood and clinker brick.

landmarks.name: Former Sigma Pi House
landmarks.subtitle: 2434 Warring Street
landmarks.blurb: A three-storey stucco Tudor Revival fraternity house on Warring Street, long the Sigma Pi chapter house, with half-timbered gables and a raised front deck.

landmarks.name: Simons Laufer Mathematical Sciences Institute
landmarks.subtitle: SLMath (formerly MSRI) · 1985
landmarks.blurb: Founded in 1982 as the Mathematical Sciences Research Institute, this independent institute hosts mathematicians from around the world for semester-long research programs, in a hillside building above the campus.

landmarks.name: Slottman Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 1
landmarks.blurb: A newer residence hall added to Unit 1 in the 2000s along Durant Avenue, with stepped colour-blocked wings and glazed stair and lounge stacks.

landmarks.name: Social Sciences Building
landmarks.subtitle: Formerly Barrows Hall · 1964
landmarks.blurb: Home to economics, political science, sociology and other social science departments, this eight-storey slab with its deep concrete sunshade grid was known as Barrows Hall until 2020, when the university removed the name of David Prescott Barrows.

landmarks.name: Soda Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Computer Science · 1994
landmarks.blurb: Home of computer science in Berkeley EECS, opened in 1994 and named for the Soda family whose foundation funded it. Its mottled glazed-tile skin, maroon stripes and top-floor arcade of open arches facing Hearst Avenue make it one of the most distinctive buildings on the north side.

landmarks.name: South Hall
landmarks.subtitle: David Farquharson · 1873
landmarks.blurb: Completed in 1873 for the College of Agriculture, South Hall is the oldest building on campus and the only survivor of the original university buildings — a rare West Coast example of the Second Empire style, now home to the School of Information.

landmarks.name: South House
landmarks.subtitle: Hillegass-Parker House · Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: South House on Parker Street is part of Hillegass-Parker House, a Berkeley Student Cooperative house.

landmarks.name: Spens-Black Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 3
landmarks.blurb: One of the four high-rise towers of Residence Halls Unit 3 on Durant Avenue, the last of the Southside 'Units' of the 1960s; its residents eat at Cafe 3.

landmarks.name: Spieker Aquatics Complex
landmarks.subtitle: Cal swimming, diving & water polo
landmarks.blurb: Home pool of Cal swimming and water polo: an outdoor 50-metre competition pool with spectator stands, next to the Recreational Sports Facility.

landmarks.name: Spieker Aquatics Complex
landmarks.subtitle: Cal swimming, diving & water polo
landmarks.blurb: Home pool of Cal swimming and water polo: an outdoor 50-metre competition pool with spectator stands, next to the Recreational Sports Facility.

landmarks.name: Sproul Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Arthur Brown Jr. · 1941
landmarks.blurb: Named for UC president Robert Gordon Sproul, this neoclassical granite-faced building housed the campus administration. In 1964 Mario Savio spoke from its steps during the Free Speech Movement; they are now the Mario Savio Steps.

landmarks.name: Stadium Parking Garage
landmarks.subtitle: Maxwell Garage · Maxwell Family Field on the roof
landmarks.blurb: A two-level parking garage next to California Memorial Stadium. Its roof is Maxwell Family Field, an artificial-turf practice field for Cal football, field hockey and lacrosse.

landmarks.name: Stanley Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Biosciences & bioengineering · 2007
landmarks.blurb: Rebuilt in 2007 on the site of the original Stanley Hall (named for biochemist Wendell Stanley), it houses bioengineering labs and the Berkeley arm of the California Institute for Quantitative Biosciences (QB3).

landmarks.name: Stebbins Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: A four-storey Berkeley Student Cooperative house on Ridge Road, one of several co-ops clustered on Northside just above campus.

landmarks.name: Stephens Hall
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1923
landmarks.blurb: Opened in 1923 as the Stephens Memorial Union, the first student union on campus, this Collegiate Gothic building beside Strawberry Creek is named for history professor Henry Morse Stephens and now houses International & Area Studies and the Academic Senate.

landmarks.name: Stern Hall
landmarks.subtitle: 1942 · Hearst Avenue at Highland Place
landmarks.blurb: Built in 1942 with a gift from Rosalie Meyer Stern in memory of her husband Sigmund Stern (class of 1879), Stern Hall opened for 90 women and is the sister hall to Bowles Hall.

landmarks.name: Strawberry Canyon Pool
landmarks.subtitle: Strawberry Canyon Recreational Area
landmarks.blurb: The outdoor pool of the Strawberry Canyon Recreational Area, set among redwoods and eucalyptus in the canyon east of Memorial Stadium, next to the Haas Clubhouse.

landmarks.name: Haas Student Services Building
landmarks.subtitle: Haas School of Business · Moore Ruble Yudell · 1995
landmarks.blurb: Part of the Haas School of Business complex designed by Charles Moore with Moore Ruble Yudell, arranged around a hillside courtyard at the east edge of campus.

landmarks.name: Clark Kerr Campus Suites
landmarks.subtitle: Clark Kerr Campus
landmarks.blurb: One of the Spanish Colonial Revival buildings of the Clark Kerr Campus, the former California Schools for the Deaf and Blind, which UC Berkeley turned into a residential campus at the foot of the hills.

landmarks.name: Sutardja Dai Hall
landmarks.subtitle: CITRIS headquarters · 2009
landmarks.blurb: Home of CITRIS (the Center for Information Technology Research in the Interest of Society) and the Banatao Institute, with the Marvell Nanofabrication Laboratory and the Banatao Auditorium. It is named for Marvell founders Sehat Sutardja and Weili Dai.

landmarks.name: Tan Hall
landmarks.subtitle: College of Chemistry · 1997
landmarks.blurb: An eight-storey research building for the College of Chemistry, named for the Tan family whose gift helped fund it. Its labs and offices complete the chemistry complex next to Latimer and Gilman halls.

landmarks.name: Tang Center
landmarks.subtitle: University Health Services
landmarks.blurb: The Tang Center houses University Health Services: the campus clinic, pharmacy, and counseling and psychological services for UC Berkeley students.

landmarks.name: Tellefsen Hall
landmarks.subtitle: 1755 Le Roy Avenue
landmarks.blurb: A university residence hall on Le Roy Avenue on Northside, long associated with the Cal Band.

landmarks.name: The Gateway
landmarks.subtitle: Barbara and Gerson Bakar Gateway · Weiss/Manfredi with Gensler · 2026
landmarks.blurb: Opened in 2026 on the former Tolman Hall site at Hearst Avenue and Arch Street, the 367,000 sq ft Bakar Gateway is the home of the College of Computing, Data Science, and Society, Berkeley's first new college in more than 50 years.

landmarks.name: The Law Building
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Law · 1951
landmarks.blurb: Home of the UC Berkeley School of Law. Opened in 1951 as Boalt Hall, it was renamed the Law Building in 2020; quotations from Justices Cardozo and Holmes are carved over its entrances.

landmarks.name: Theta Chi
landmarks.subtitle: ΘΧ · 2499 Piedmont Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house of Theta Chi at Piedmont Avenue and Dwight Way, a white stucco Mediterranean house with low hipped roofs and red letters over the door.

landmarks.name: Theta Xi
landmarks.subtitle: ΘΞ · 2639 Durant Avenue
landmarks.blurb: Theta Xi chapter house on Durant Avenue, a front-gabled Arts-and-Crafts house in cream stucco with a columned front porch.

landmarks.name: Towle Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Residence Halls Unit 2
landmarks.blurb: A newer residence hall added to Unit 2 in the 2000s; it is Christian Hall's twin, with lower colour-blocked wings and glazed stair and lounge stacks between the 1960s towers.

landmarks.name: Edwards Stadium track
landmarks.subtitle: 400 m · 8 lanes
landmarks.blurb: The oval at Edwards Stadium, where Cal track and field competes; the stadium hosted the NCAA championships and a run of world records in the 1960s and 70s.

landmarks.name: Undergraduate Academic Building
landmarks.subtitle: Mass timber · 2026
landmarks.blurb: Opened for the fall 2026 semester, this five-storey hub of classrooms, a 400-seat auditorium and a rooftop terrace is the first mass-timber building on the Berkeley campus.

landmarks.name: Underhill Parking & Field
landmarks.subtitle: Parking garage with a rooftop field
landmarks.blurb: A UC Berkeley parking garage of about 950 spaces, mostly below grade, topped by Underhill Field, a lit artificial-turf field used by Cal field hockey and intramural sports.

landmarks.name: University House
landmarks.subtitle: Albert Pissis · 1911
landmarks.blurb: Built as the residence of University of California presidents and later home to Berkeley's chancellors, this sandstone Italian Renaissance villa stands in its own garden at the northwest corner of campus.

landmarks.name: Upper Hearst Parking Structure
landmarks.subtitle: Parking structure · tennis courts on the roof
landmarks.blurb: A UC Berkeley parking structure of about 400 spaces on Hearst Avenue, with tennis courts on its roof deck.

landmarks.name: Valley Life Sciences Building
landmarks.subtitle: George W. Kelham · 1930
landmarks.blurb: Opened in 1930 as the Life Sciences Building, this enormous Art Deco block is decorated with friezes of plants and animals. Renovated and renamed for Wayne and Gladys Valley in the 1990s, it houses the UC Museum of Paleontology, whose T. rex cast stands in the atrium.

landmarks.name: Weill Hall
landmarks.subtitle: Molecular & Cell Biology
landmarks.blurb: Built as the Life Sciences Addition and part of a major campus drive to improve facilities for biology, the six-story Weill Hall houses 46 laboratory suites for advanced biological research.

landmarks.name: Wellman Hall
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1912
landmarks.blurb: Built as Agriculture Hall, the first of Howard's agricultural group on the west side of campus, and later renamed for UC president Harry R. Wellman, an agricultural economist.

landmarks.name: Wheeler Hall
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1917
landmarks.blurb: Named for university president Benjamin Ide Wheeler, this granite Classical Revival hall houses Wheeler Auditorium, the largest lecture hall on campus, where Ernest O. Lawrence received his 1939 Nobel Prize in Physics in February 1940.

landmarks.name: Witter Rugby Field
landmarks.subtitle: Cal Rugby · Strawberry Canyon
landmarks.blurb: The home pitch of Cal Rugby, one of the most successful programs in college rugby, set in Strawberry Canyon just east of Memorial Stadium.

landmarks.name: Wolf House
landmarks.subtitle: Berkeley Student Cooperative
landmarks.blurb: A cream-and-blue stucco co-op house on Durant Avenue, a block east of campus, run by the Berkeley Student Cooperative.

landmarks.name: Women's Faculty Club
landmarks.subtitle: John Galen Howard · 1923
landmarks.blurb: Founded by women faculty and staff who were not admitted to the Faculty Club, this brown-shingled clubhouse beside Strawberry Creek has hosted members and overnight guests since 1923.

landmarks.name: Zellerbach Hall
landmarks.subtitle: DeMars & Hardison · 1968
landmarks.blurb: Home of Cal Performances, Zellerbach Hall seats about 2,000 for concerts, dance and theatre. Its concrete-framed glass lobby closes the west side of Lower Sproul Plaza.

landmarks.name: Zellerbach Playhouse
landmarks.subtitle: DeMars & Hardison · 1968
landmarks.blurb: The Playhouse is the smaller theatre of the Zellerbach complex, used for Theater, Dance & Performance Studies productions and Cal Performances events.

landmarks.name: Zeta Psi
landmarks.subtitle: ΖΨ · 2728 Bancroft Way
landmarks.blurb: Chapter house of the Iota chapter of Zeta Psi on Bancroft Way, a long two-storey mid-century house with a brick ground floor and a cantilevered panelled upper storey.
